messages:
olivia: noticing a sharp latency spike for text-generation in eu-east1 around 09:12 UTC, p50 jumped from ~60ms to ~700ms
deploy-bot: alert: service=text-gen region=eu-east1 severity=high latency_p95=820ms
sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1734, paging oncall cheng
cheng: on it, checking hotpool and batcher metrics now
akash: opening runtime dashboard — looks like batching queue depth exploded, many requests sitting in slowpath, KV cache hit-rate dropped ~30%
maria: infra metrics show node-level IO waits on hotpool eu-east1-hot-3, GPU utilization is moderate though (~55%)
cheng: can we get a quick stacktrace or runtime logs from a sample replica?
akash: pasting tail of runtime log sample:
```
[09:11:58] batcher: enqueue request id=0x7f3a size=512
[09:12:02] kvcache: miss prefix="/embeds/" key=0x1a2b
[09:12:02] scheduler: request stalled in slowpath > 3.5s
[09:12:05] batcher: flush window triggered (150ms) length=1
[09:12:10] rpc: retrying to backend due to timeout
```
akash: looks like continuous batching slowpath + kvcache decompaction timing causing stalls
leo: routing team — how hard to shift some traffic off eu-east1 to na1 for frontend customers?
tim: we have spare capacity in na1 and eu-west1 but cross-region adds latency for EU users; we can divert non-SLA traffic (lower tier) to na1 now
maya: cost note: cross-region live routing will increase egress and inter-region costs, expecting an extra ~$4k/day at current rates if we keep >20% diverted
cheng: prioritize availability, we can tighten filters to only divert background and non-interactive paths first
akash: quick mitigation plan: 1) disable continuous batching slowpath flag 2) reduce batch window from 150ms -> 40ms 3) temporarily increase KV worker pool to speed compaction
maria: infra ops: starting node drain on eu-east1-hot-3 (suspected IO noisy neighbor), will rebalance before killing any pods
leo: initiating routing policy change: divert 30% of low-priority traffic eu-east1 -> na1 now. applying rollout: 5% -> 15% -> 30% over 3m
cheng: deploying akash's runtime flag change (runtime.disable_continuous_slowpath=true) to one canary node
akash: canary applied to eu-east1-hot-1, observing metrics
akash: canary: p50 from 720ms -> 190ms in 45s :thumbsup:
maria: drain completed on eu-east1-hot-3, removing from routing pool, redistributing workloads
leo: rollout now at 15% -> increasing to 30%
maya: accounting FYI: divert hit estimate updated to ~$1.6k/day at 30%
tim: also bumped batcher concurrency config: max_inflight 64 -> 96 to absorb bursts, will monitor memory pressure
akash: increased kv worker threads from 4 -> 8 on canary, compaction latency started improving
cheng: after changes p95 in eu-east1 down from 820ms -> 240ms, p50 ~100-140ms
olivia: customers are still seeing occasional tail spikes, are we confident rollback is not needed?
akash: initial suspect was a recent kernel-level micro-optim change that altered kernel selector heuristics, but the runtime flag avoids slowpath so rollback not immediate required
maria: we've reclaimed one noisy node and added 2 spare gpus in eu-west to help routing soak, autoscaler will keep a watch
leo: routing steering: keeping 30% diverted for the next 20m, we can scale down if steady
cheng: assigning action items: akash to instrument a finer KV cache metric, maria to run node postmortem, leo to update routing policy doc, olivia to draft incident comms
olivia: drafting short note for customers: "We observed degraded latency in EU region, mitigations in place, some traffic temporarily routed to alternate regions. Working on full root cause and will follow up."
maya: please add estimated cost impact to ops incident ticket INC-2026-1734
akash: pushing a canary-wide rollout of runtime.disable_continuous_slowpath=true across eu-east1 now
akash: rollout complete, p95 stable ~170-220ms, no new slowpath logs after 2m
cheng: reducing diverted traffic 30% -> 10% over 2m
leo: diverted traffic now at 10% and decreasing
maria: hotpool rebalance finished, no more IO anomalies on eu-east1 nodes
cheng: marking incident as mitigated in the channel, keeping SEV open for monitoring for 2 hours
olivia: thanks all. postmortem lead: maria, expected draft in 48h
maya: noted cost of emergency capacity and inter-region egress, adding to postmortem
akash: will follow up with a perf test to validate batcher heuristics and add a guard to prevent slowpath regressions
cheng: closing loop: INC-2026-1734 -> state=mitigated, oncall=cheng, severity=SEV2
olivia: reaction :heart: on the quick turnaround, good job everyone
